prompt:
Create a pixel-art atlas from the supplied exact reference, exactly 2-by-2 equal cells, each portrait-eye crop 64:35, total 128:70 (64:35). No gutters, text, borders or extra panels. Top-left: same face looking gently LEFT with eyes open. Top-right: same face looking gently RIGHT with eyes open. Bottom-left: LEFT with eyes half-lidded. Bottom-right: RIGHT with eyes half-lidded.

Use the supplied grid as the exact identity and anatomy reference. Preserve the angry expression, brow shapes and positions, eye spacing, face crop, hair and skin colors, eyelid contours and lash lines. Keep the exact aperture: open cells match the source open row; half-lidded cells match the source half row. Preserve the source's compact muted green iris color and dark stepped pupils. Both eyes look in the same requested direction, with only a subtle lateral shift of about one native pixel. Keep irises compact, naturally stepped and fully inside the existing lid openings. Sclera remains muted and warm beige/tan; no broad white bands. Highlights stay tiny and dim, with no bright glare.

Maintain crisp native pixel-art steps and source palette; do not smooth or vectorize. Do not widen or raise the eyes, change eyelid shape/aperture, enlarge or round irises, recolor eyes, add glints, change the brows or expression, or alter other face details. Bottom cells differ from their top counterparts only by exact half-lid aperture and subtle horizontal glance.
